name: sshi_fbr
rationale: The piezo open-circuit voltage (0.76 V) is too low to efficiently overcome the diode drops of a full-bridge rectifier (FBR) and reach the 1.8 V goal. I am implementing a Synchronous Switch Harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) topology. By using an inductor and a switch to flip the voltage on the piezo capacitance at the extrema, we can significantly increase the effective voltage amplitude seen by the rectifier, allowing the output to reach 1.8 V even under weak excitation (S4) and heavy load (S2). A Zener clamp is added to ensure vout_max <= 3.6 V.

name: sece_inductive
rationale: Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) is often more effective than SSHI for very low voltage sources. This topology uses switches to disconnect the piezo and extract its charge through an inductor into the storage capacitor at the voltage peaks. This acts as an inductive boost, which can more aggressively step up the voltage to the 1.8 V - 3.6 V range.

name: sshi_half_bridge
rationale: A variant of the SSHI but using a half-wave rectifier. This reduces the total diode voltage drop from 0.5 V to 0.25 V on the conduction path, which may improve startup time (tup) and settled voltage (vavg) in the weakest conditions (S4, S6) by reducing losses.

name: s_sshi_transfer
rationale: The previous sshi_fbr failed to reach 1.8V on weak conditions (S4, S5, S6) due to the 0.5V drop of the full-bridge rectifier. This new topology implements a Synchronous-Transfer SSHI: it uses the same L-S flip circuit to boost the voltage across the piezo, but instead of a full bridge, it uses two diodes and a synchronous switch to transfer the charge to the output. This reduces the conduction loss from two diode drops to one, significantly increasing the available power for the load and enabling the output to reach the 1.8V threshold even under weak excitation.

name: sshi_half_bridge
rationale: The previous 'sshi_fbr' design failed on ripple and settling on the weakest conditions (S4) because the storage capacitor C1 had to be kept small to meet the startup time (tup) requirement. However, the Full Bridge Rectifier (FBR) introduces two diode drops, significantly reducing efficiency. By tying pzn to ground (creating a half-bridge configuration), we reduce the rectification loss to a single diode drop. This increase in delivered voltage and current allows us to use a larger C1 to suppress ripple and stabilize the output (reducing dv) while still meeting the startup time constraint.

name: sshi_fbr_lc
rationale: The previous SSHI-FBR (c0012) nearly met all goals but struggled with the tradeoff between output ripple (vpp) and settling time (dv), especially on light loads (S3, S4). To decouple these, I am adding a filter inductor L2 between the full-bridge rectifier and the storage capacitor C1. This LC filter significantly reduces the peak-to-peak ripple without requiring a large C1, which in turn allows for a smaller time constant to improve the settling time (dv) and ensure the startup time (tup) remains within the 0.4s limit for S4.

name: sshi_fbr_pi
rationale: The previous best design (sshi_fbr_lc) is extremely close to passing, failing only on the S3 ripple constraint (51.5 mV vs 50 mV). This ripple is caused by the high charging pulses of the strong excitation in S3. To reduce ripple without significantly increasing the startup time (tup) or the settling time (dv), I am adding a pre-filter capacitor (C_pre) at the output of the full-bridge rectifier. This transforms the existing L-C filter into a C-L-C pi-filter, which provides significantly better ripple rejection for the same total capacitance, allowing the optimizer to find a balance between S3 ripple and S4 startup/settling requirements.
